business-review.name: Business Review
business-review.summary: Full-loop review of recent activities to identify achievements, address challenges, and plan improvements. Goes deeper than a status update — closer to a customer-facing or partner-facing relationship review.

beats.name: Logo
beats.description: Cover slide with logos and the review period. Establishes brand identity and signals the level of formality the rest of the deck will hold to.

beats.name: Opening
beats.description: Frame the meeting context and the goals for the next hour. What you'll cover, what decisions you want, what you don't intend to relitigate.

beats.name: Review
beats.description: Outline the recent activities in scope: launches, projects, programs. Just enough scope-setting that the rest of the deck has shared vocabulary.

beats.name: Successes
beats.description: Recognize the achievements in the review window. Lead with outcomes the audience cares about, not effort. Specific moves earn more credibility than aggregate progress.

beats.name: Challenges
beats.description: Address the problems faced honestly. What didn't work, what's still hard. Naming challenges in front of the audience earns more trust than letting them ask.

beats.name: Solutions
beats.description: Discuss the fixes already implemented. Pair each with the result it produced, or, if it's still in flight, with the leading indicator you're watching.

beats.name: Outcome
beats.description: Display the results achieved across the review window. Let the data carry the slide; supporting commentary should explain context, not inflate the numbers.

beats.name: Insights
beats.description: Highlight the key learnings. What was confirmed, what surprised you, what the audience should take away. Insights are the slides people quote in follow-on meetings.

beats.name: Future Strategy
beats.description: Define the next steps and the strategic direction that follows from the review. Specific enough to sequence; flexible enough to adapt.

beats.name: Feedback
beats.description: Capture audience thoughts. Two or three explicit prompts where you want input or alignment. The strength of a relationship review is in the conversation it provokes.

beats.name: Next Review
beats.description: Plan for follow-up: when the next review happens, what evidence you'll bring, what decisions are deferred until then. Continuity is the point of the cadence.

beats.name: Closing
beats.description: Recap and express optimism about the path forward. Close with the next concrete step and the people responsible for it.

board.name: Board of Directors
board.summary: Directors with fiduciary responsibility who balance oversight, advice, and approval.
board.description: The board is governance-first. They want a complete picture: financial health, key metrics, functional updates, risks, and forward-looking topics. Surface bad news honestly — under-disclosure erodes trust faster than the problems themselves. Bring specific asks that turn the meeting into a working session rather than a recital.

executive.name: Executive
executive.summary: C-suite and senior leadership focused on strategic decisions, ROI, and big-picture outcomes. Highly time-constrained.
executive.description: C-suite and senior leaders deciding on strategy, ROI, and big-picture outcomes with very little time. Lead with the conclusion and keep to one insight per slide; set the key numbers in bold type and use as few bullet points as possible. Keep chart density low and the deck to 10-15 slides at most.

educate.name: Educate
educate.summary: Teach a concept, process, product, or domain so the audience can use it correctly.
educate.description: Use when the primary job is learning. Structure around concepts, examples, practice, and checks for understanding rather than persuasion or reporting.
educate.outcome: The audience understands the material well enough to apply it.

conversational.name: Conversational
conversational.summary: Direct, dialog-style voice for podcasts, fireside chats, and small-group reviews.
conversational.description: Sound like one half of a real conversation. Ask questions on the slide and answer them; keep paragraphs short; lean into examples over abstractions. Useful when the deck is meant to support a discussion rather than to lecture.
voiceCues: Ask a question on the slide, then answer it on the next.
Use second person — speak to the room, not at it.
Lean on stories and concrete examples over abstract framing.
Keep each idea to one short paragraph; let the dialog do the rest.
avoid: Stuffing slides — leave room for the discussion.
Inside-baseball references the room may not share.
samplePhrases: Why now? Two things changed in the last six months.
Here's the part that surprised us — and what we did about it.
If you take one thing from this section, take this.

classic.name: Classic
classic.description: A timeless, clean, and versatile theme with balanced color contrasts and classic typography. Ideal for professional, readable presentations.

boost.name: Boost
boost.summary: High-energy digital accents for demos and launch moments.
boost.description: A vivid blue-red digital palette with bright chart accents. Best for product stories that need strong on-screen presence.

cool-horizon.name: Cool Horizon
cool-horizon.summary: Cool blue-green palette tuned for professional business decks.
cool-horizon.description: A balanced cool-toned scheme with deep navy, business blues, and teal accents. It works well across strategy, finance, and technical narratives.

aptos.name: Aptos
aptos.description: Aptos is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Aptos Display for headings with Aptos for body text.

tenorite.name: Tenorite
tenorite.description: Tenorite is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Tenorite Display for headings with Tenorite for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

table-beside.name: Table beside
table-beside.summary: A table with commentary beside it.
table-beside.description: Place a table beside its interpretation. Use the supporting text to explain the conclusion without repeating every cell.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.summary: Dated events or a roadmap along one axis, with optional notes.
timeline.description: Show events or milestones in chronological order. Label each item with a date or stage and a concise description.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
